item.title: FCA bans trio behind £35.5m scheme designed to bypass visa rules
item.description: The FCA has decided to ban 3 former senior figures at Dolfin Financial (UK) Limited (Dolfin) after finding they ran a scheme that helped clients bypass UK visa rules. These individuals ran a scheme designed to get around the UK's investor visa rules, undermining their purpose of attracting genuine investment into the UK. Between 2016 and 2019, most clients using the scheme paid a fee of £400,000 instead of investing £2m of their own money in UK companies, as required under the Home Office investor visa rules.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Legal Tech Funding Down Slightly From All-Time High
item.description: If AI legal tech funding was a baseball game, this might be roughly the fifth inning. In the past two years, venture investors have poured more than $7 billion into legal and legal tech startups, most with an AI focus. So far this year, legal tech startups have pulled in more than $2.2 billion.

item.title: Third-party capital around one-third of global life annuity reinsurance capacity: AM Best & GC
item.description: In a new report this morning, rating agency AM Best highlights the expansive global life and annuity reinsurance space saying it is “well capitalized and positioned for robust growth due to increased dedicated capital for life reinsurance for traditional life business and more asset-intensive annuity business via third-party capital.” After which it provides the estimate from the reinsurance broker, writing, “Guy Carpenter estimates that third-party capital accounted for around one-third of total capacity in 2025, which has doubled since 2022.” Which drives home the increasingly important role of third-party capital structures in the life and annuity reinsurance market around the world. As use of third-party capital within life annuity reinsurance structures including sidecar vehicles increases, a new estimate from reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, as reported by rating agency AM Best, suggests around one-third of capacity is now from third-party investor sources. In fact, this shows that third-party capital penetration into the life and annuities market has been far more rapid than in P&C reinsurance risks, where alternative or ILS capital from third-party investors remains around 18% of global dedicated reinsurance capital, according to recent data from the same pair of companies .

item.title: EIB and WFP launch parametric insurance scheme to protect Ethiopian smallholder farmers
item.description: The European Investment Bank (EIB), through its development arm EIB Global, is issuing a grant of up to €4 million to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), which will be used to support the development and rollout of parametric insurance products to protect smallholder farmers in Ethiopia. WFP will use its extensive expertise in rural finance and climate-resilience programming in Ethiopia to develop and pilot this index-based microinsurance (parametric) scheme in partnership with a number of private insurance companies. The grant will support capacity building for the Development Bank of Ethiopia, rural finance institutions and smallholder farmers, as well as the establishment of a Premium Guarantee Fund to pre-finance insurance premiums.

item.title: Swiss pension Nest says ILS investments achieved “convincing results again” in 2025
item.description: Nest Sammelstiftung, or the Nest Collective Foundation, a Swiss pension that adopts sustainable investment strategies and allocates to insurance-linked securities through a number of ILS managers has reported that its allocation achieved “convincing results” again in 2025. While on ILS specifically, the Nest pension fund explained, “Insurance Linked Securities (ILS) were again able to benefit from attractive risk premiums and achieved convincing results,” through 2025. For full-year 2025, while the investor does not provide a specific return figure for its ILS investments, the pension said the results were “convincing”.

item.title: Reinsurance capital hit record $663bn in 2025 as cat risk budgets fall: AM Best and Guy Carpenter
item.description: The report shows that dedicated reinsurance capital reached USD $663 billion at the end of 2025, according to data from AM Best and reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, while catastrophe risk budgets continued to fall. AM Best and Guy Carpenter estimate that total dedicated reinsurance capital increased from USD $607 billion at the end of 2024 to USD $663 billion at the end of 2025. The global reinsurance sector is carrying more capital than ever while allocating a smaller proportion of that capital to catastrophe risk, according to new analysis from AM Best, a global credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry data and analysis.

item.title: Strong earnings and capital give carriers more choice as rates soften: Howden Re
item.description: In Howden Re’s latest re/insurer earnings report, Michelle To, Head of Business Intelligence, said that as pricing becomes more competitive, carriers are taking a closer look at where they grow, which areas they prioritise, and how they deploy capital, with greater emphasis now on cycle management. “Strong operating performance, favourable prior-year reserve development and healthy capital positions are giving carriers choices over where to put capital next,” Howden Re said. “The half-year 2026 report looks beyond headline rate movements to assess how earnings, reserves, capital and portfolio decisions can help us prepare for the next phase of the cycle,” Howden Re explained.

item.description: Willis, a WTW business, has announced the appointment of Paul Haas as Senior Director, Business Development, based in Chicago. Having joined Willis on August 10, Haas has been tasked with leading new business development across the Midwest, with a focus on growing the company’s presence in financial institutions risk at the intersection of banking and digital assets. Ryan Pischke, Managing Director and Regional Growth Leader for the Midwest at Willis, commented: “We’re excited to welcome Paul to Willis at a time when financial institutions are navigating significant change, particularly as banking and digital assets continue to converge.

item.title: SpaceX Plans $100 Billion Louisiana Site in Post-IPO Growth Push
item.description: SpaceX plans to build a new $100 billion launch site for its Starship rocket on the southern coast of Louisiana, enabling the company to expand operations of the behemoth vehicle that’s critical to its future. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry and SpaceX executives announced the plans on Tuesday, authorizing the company to build a facility across roughly 125,000 acres (about 506 square kilometers) in a coastal area known as Pecan Island. The site will provide SpaceX with a third potential location for launching Starship, which SpaceX primarily builds and launches in South Texas.

item.title: Freestone Acquires Illinois-Based 360 Benefits
item.description: Freestone Insurance Group, a Shore Capital Partners portfolio company, has acquired 360 Benefits, an employee benefits focused brokerage based in Chicago. The transaction furthers Freestone’s Midwest presence and strengthens its existing employee benefits practice. 360 serves privately held, middle-market employers across a broad range of industries, delivering high-touch consultative benefits and risk management solutions.

item.title: INTX extends technology platform as Xitus Re expands run-off operations
item.description: INTX Insurance Software has extended its relationship with Bermuda-based property and casualty runoff reinsurer Xitus Re, with the INTX (Re)Insurance Operating System continuing to support the company as it adds portfolios, transactions, and operations across multiple jurisdictions. According to INTX, the broader deployment is intended to give Xitus a consistent technology foundation as its business develops. A key component of the deployment is INTX Re, the firm’s assumed reinsurance platform.

item.title: Marsh prepares Archer brand
item.description: Marsh McLennan appears to be preparing a new reinsurance and captive-services brand called “Archer by Marsh.” The company filed a US trademark application for the name on August 13, covering reinsurance brokerage and intermediary services, insurance administration, and the formation, structuring, and management of captive insurers and reinsurance vehicles. No public announcement or operational website for Archer by Marsh appears to have been released. Marsh has made corresponding applications outside the US.

item.description: El patrimonio bajo gestión de los planes de pensiones del Sistema Individual se redujo un 0,62% en el mes de julio, hasta un total gestionado en 93.263 millones de euros, según Vdos. Por tipo de entidad, los grupos internacionales han registrado el mayor incremento patrimonial en el mes en términos porcentuales, con un 1,29%.

item.description: La Comisión Europea ha solicitado a Eiopa que le ofrezca asesoramiento técnico sobre el posible contenido de actos delegados de la Directiva de Distribución de Seguros (IDD), en el contexto de la Estrategia de Inversión Minorista (RIS). item.title: El capital reasegurador mundial alcanza un máximo histórico de 663.000 millones de dólares en 2025
item.description: El capital dedicado al mercado reasegurador mundial alcanzó los 663.000 millones de dólares a cierre de 2025, frente a 607.000 millones el año anterior, según un informe de AM Best y Guy Carpenter publicado el 14 de agosto.

item.title: AI Firms Debate Putting Cyber Tests Online After Model Hacks
item.description: Artificial intelligence labs and cybersecurity firms are reconsidering the way they test advanced AI models after models from at least three firms jumped onto the open internet and breached real-world victims. That would mark a major shift, after technology firms for a generation have isolated their sandboxes in order to be sure that their software – whether it be malware samples or mobile apps – can’t cause collateral damage. Related: Allstate Introduces Large Language Model, ALLIE The conversation intensified after OpenAI disclosed that some of its most advanced models had escaped a sandbox, accessed the internet, broken into another company’s servers and stolen confidential information.

item.title: Canada Slaps Retaliatory Tariffs on US Goods Worth $20B as Trade War Intensifies
item.description: Canada’s retaliatory tariffs, calculated using 2024 trade figures, cover goods accounting for nearly 4.5% of Canada’s imports from the United States. Canada hit back on Tuesday with retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. The new tit-for-tat tariffs mark a new low in relations between the longtime allies, and Trump earlier on Tuesday threatened to rename Lake Ontario, which straddles both countries, “Lake America.” “Our dollar-for-dollar, rate for rate counter-tariffs as well as a multi-billion dollar support package will protect workers, farmers, families, and businesses,” Canada’s Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said.

item.title: Deloitte to Pay $21.5 Million to Settle US Probe Over DEI
item.description: Accounting firm Deloitte will pay $21.5 million to settle a U.S. Department of Justice probe over diversity, equity and inclusion practices , which President Donald Trump’s administration has cracked down on during his second term in office. The Trump administration has targeted public and private organizations, from government agencies to universities, over DEI practices that civil rights advocates say help address historic inequities for marginalized groups like women, the LGBT community and ethnic minorities.

item.title: Gatik raises $200 million
item.description: Self-driving trucking startup Gatik announced $200 million in Series D funding led by Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with participation from Millennium Management, ARK Invest, Intact Private Capital and others. Founded in 2017, Gatik has built “one of the most commercially advanced” businesses in autonomous freight, with more than $600 million in contracted revenue, 85,000 fully driverless orders completed, and 99% on-time delivery across its operations. “This round, led by some of the world’s leading financial institutions, is a clear validation of Gatik’s commercial leadership in autonomous freight.

item.title: CTC Insurance Brings Direct Bill Reconciliation Fully In-House with Applied Recon
item.description: “Bringing that process in-house with Applied Recon means CTC Insurance’s finance team knows exactly where every dollar stands the moment it moves, so they catch a mismatch the day it happens instead of finding out at month-end close.” The post CTC Insurance Brings Direct Bill Reconciliation Fully In-House with Applied Recon appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . Applied Systems ® announced that CTC Insurance, a full-service insurance agency founded in 1913, has selected Applied Recon to bring its direct bill reconciliation entirely in-house, eliminating its reliance on outsourced manual processing. “With Applied Recon’s smart matching clearing items straight off the suspense list, my team isn’t stuck re-searching the same policies month after month, and we always know exactly where every reconciliation stands instead of waiting on someone outside our office to tell us.” Applied Recon is an AI-powered reconciliation capability built into Applied’s insurance management systems that automates the matching of direct bill statements to agency records.

item.title: UNICO Group acquires Oracle Insurance Agency
item.description: Nebraska-based insurance brokerage UNICO Group has acquired Oracle Insurance Agency. Oracle’s clients will gain access to UNICO’s broader capabilities across property and casualty insurance, employee benefits, risk management and business solutions. Founded in 2010 by Wil and Denise Stephany, Omaha-based Oracle specializes in personal lines and private client insurance.

item.title: Judge Approves $117.5 Million Settlement in ‘Complex’ Comcast Data Breach Case
item.description: A federal judge has approved a $117.5 million data breach settlement against Comcast Cable Communications. The agreement represents one of the largest data breach settlement amounts and, with 31.7 million potential members, one of the largest classes in a data breach case. The case also represents one of the more complex data breach cases to date, according to Judge John Younge of the U.S.

item.title: Chronic Traumatic Brain Damage Widespread in Former NFL Athletes
item.description: Almost every former National Football League player who died between 2016 and 2021 and allowed their brains to be evaluated were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy, stark evidence of the toll repeated head impacts can take on athletes. Researchers obtained personal information and causes of death for 878 players who died during the five-year period, when brain donations were highest. Of the 235 athletes whose brains were subject to the postmortem neurological examination, 215 had confirmed CTE, according to findings published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal.

item.title: Backcountry Guide Company Faces $150K Fine After Deadly California Avalanche
item.description: California workplace safety officials have fined a guide company that was leading backcountry skiers down a mountain in February when an avalanche was triggered, killing nine members of the group in the deadliest avalanche in the state’s modern history. The largest fine, $81,000, was for “failing to correct the imminent hazard posed by traveling in avalanche terrain when the avalanche danger was rated high.” The agency issued the fines earlier this month. The nine people who died were part of a group of 15 backcountry skiers headed out on a three-day trek organized by Blackbird Mountain Guides into pristine wilderness near Frog Lake in California’s Sierra Nevada as a powerful winter storm moved into the state.

item.title: What We Know About the Door Handles That Triggered China’s Record Auto Recall
item.description: Electronic door handles of the kind that are at the center of China’s largest-ever vehicle recall have proliferated across the globe over the past decade, especially on electric vehicles. Tesla and eight other automakers said on Friday they will recall a total of about 4.3 million vehicles in China over concerns that their doors may be difficult to open in an emergency. Popularized by Tesla, the door handles are designed to sit flush to the body of the door, for a minimalist look that also reduces aerodynamic drag.

item.title: Florida Man Arrested for $206K Luxury Vehicle Insurance Fraud Scheme
item.description: A Florida man was arrested after fraudulently submitting 41 vehicle insurance applications on luxury vehicles that he never owned, according to an announcement yesterday by the state’s Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia. Arrested earlier this month, he faces the following charges: organized scheme to defraud, insurance fraud, grand theft, and fraudulent use of personal identification. The Department of Financial Services Criminal Investigations Division (CID) investigators discovered that the man, Adam Otrok, used counterfeit and fictitious personal identification information to submit vehicle insurance applications.

item.title: ILS and broader securitisation key to absorbing nat cat risk: Schroders Capital
item.description: The increasing need for capital to manage and mitigate natural hazard risk is creating strong opportunities for investors, according to Schroders Capital, who emphasises that by allocating to catastrophe risk through insurance-linked securities, broader securitisation, and other risk-transfer markets, investors can secure attractive returns by absorbing catastrophe risk when pricing reflects expected losses and required margin. As natural hazard risk continues to intensify, Schroders Capital notes that the capital markets are increasingly being recognised as not only being a mechanism for absorbing financial losses, but also as a key source of financing for adaptation and resiliency. “Given the insurance industry’s enabling role for other economic activities, that approach should be closer to the way insurance has assessed risk: probabilistically, distribution-based, and with explicit acknowledgement of uncertainty,” Schroders Capital said.

item.title: MS Amlin adds Alex Jomaa and Monica Tigleanu to cyber team
item.description: MS Amlin, a global specialty commercial insurance and reinsurance provider and part of MS&AD, has appointed Alex Jomaa as Head of Cyber and Monica Tigleanu as Lead Underwriter. In the new role, Jomaa will report to Stuart Wood, Director of Casualty and Cyber, MS Amlin. MS Amlin began writing cyber treaty in 2024, and expanded into direct cyber insurance in 2025 through a small number of strategic coverholder relationships.

item.title: Asia reinsurance market resilient as abundant capacity softens rates: AM Best
item.description: The Asian reinsurance market experienced abundant capacity, sliding rates, and over-placement during the 2026 renewal season, mirroring the same broad theme seen across the global reinsurance market, AM Best noted in a recent report. While this capacity has not materially disrupted market dynamics, early activity has been observed primarily in facultative and specialty lines, AM Best noted. Despite downward pricing pressure, cedents maintained largely stable deductibles, using ceded premium savings to buy up higher-layered limits and back emerging lines with growing risk appetites, according to AM Best’s AsiaFocus: Resilience Through Transformation report.

item.title: Missouri Contractor Sentenced for Fraud Scheme
item.description: Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced that a contractor has pled guilty to defrauding consumers through his residential contracting business. As part of his guilty plea, Matlock was sentenced to four years in prison on the deceptive business practices conviction and five years on the stealing conviction. Matlock, owner of Matlock Construction, pled guilty on August 17 to one felony count of deceptive business practices and one felony count of stealing.

item.title: People Moves: Alacrity Solutions Promotes Boyd to COO
item.description: Alacrity Solutions Group LLC , headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, promoted Lee Boyd to chief operating officer (COO). Backed by over two decades of experience in the insurance industry, Boyd joined Alacrity in 2021 and has held the roles of vice president of TPA Operations and, most recently, president of claims operations. As COO, Boyd oversees Alacrity’s operational strategy across claims and business functions, working closely with the executive leadership team to drive efficiency, scale technology initiatives, and support the company’s long-term strategic objectives.

item.title: Google Expands Gemini Enterprise AI Platform for Law Firms, Lawyers
item.description: Alphabet’s Google on Tuesday expanded its Gemini Enterprise artificial intelligence platform with new tools for lawyers and law firms, accelerating a race among technology companies to meet legal sector demand for AI. The company said its Gemini Enterprise for Legal would help law firms use AI to manage routine and complex work to allow lawyers to focus on higher-value services , while keeping their data secure and confidential. The new plug-in for Gemini Enterprise includes integration with legal software and data platforms and a stable of AI agents that Google said can handle specialized legal and administrative functions without significant human oversight.

item.title: $900m partnership: Sun Life and Wilton Re to launch Windsor Life Re reinsurer
item.description: As part of the deal, Wilton Re will establish Windsor Life Re, a US and Bermuda-domiciled reinsurer supporting growth of Wilton Re’s core in-force life and annuity block origination in the US. Sun Life Financial and Wilton Re have entered into a definitive agreement to establish a strategic reinsurance and asset management partnership, combining Wilton Re’s liability management expertise with Sun Life’s insurance and asset management capabilities. Under the terms of the agreement, Windsor Life Re will reinsure from Wilton Re an initial in-force block of approximately $1.7bn, with future business ceded by Wilton Re on a quota share basis.

item.title: ANV to acquire vehicle warranty MGA Car Care Plan from AmTrust
item.description: Insurance intermediary platform ANV Group Holdings has agreed to acquire UK-based vehicle warranty MGA Car Care Plan from AmTrust Financial Services. Founded in 1976, Car Care Plan provides vehicle warranties, asset protection products, and after-sales administration to more than 30 automakers and over 2,500 dealers. The transaction also includes Car Care Plan’s overseas subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Turkey, and China, as well as Dent Wizard Ventures, a UK provider of mobile bodywork, paint, and alloy-wheel repair services.

item.title: AUB Group international profit jumps 19.6% as UK retail platform scales
item.description: AUB Group’s International division was the standout performer in the group’s FY26 results, released to the Australian Securities Exchange today, lifting underlying net profit before tax 19.6% to A$124.5m and expanding EBIT margin by 410 basis points to 27.6%. The division houses Lloyd’s wholesale broker Tysers and the group’s expanding UK retail operations. At group level, AUB reported underlying net profit after tax of A$224.6m, up 12.2%, on revenue of A$1,596.6m.
